The drawing shows an isoxazole ring with these atoms and substituents:

- The ring atoms are N, O, C5, C4 and C3.
- N is bonded to O.
- C3 bears a phenyl group and is double-bonded to N.
- C4 bears a 4-nitrophenyl group.
- C5 bears a methyl group and is double-bonded to C4. It is also bonded to O.

Writing this out as SMILES: Cc1onc(-c2ccccc2)c1-c1ccc(cc1)[N+](=O)[O-]

Checking the ring closure: c1 (C5, with methyl), o, n, c (C3, with phenyl), c1 (C4, with nitrophenyl) closes back to C5. This is a five-membered ring, as drawn. The nitro group is written in its charged form, [N+](=O)[O-].

The structure is 5-methyl-4-(4-nitrophenyl)-3-phenylisoxazole. The drawing has no wedges, hashes or cis/trans geometry, so no stereochemistry is included.

SMILES: Cc1onc(-c2ccccc2)c1-c1ccc(cc1)[N+](=O)[O-]
